match.reason: The bank point covers the Soviet Five-Year Plans from 1928 in general, while the new point is China's First Five-Year Plan of the 1950s, so it is a related but narrower and different case that would need a rewritten card rather than small changes.

draft.title: The first Five-Year Plan
card: The first Five-Year Plan ran from 1953 to 1957. The state set output targets for the whole economy, a method called central planning.
The plan copied the Soviet Union's model. It put most investment into heavy industry, such as steel, coal and machinery.
The Soviet Union sent advisers and equipment, and many large factories were built with its help. Farming and light industry received far less investment.
Industrial output grew quickly. Most new investment went to cities, and the plan did little to raise farm output.
draft.remember: The plan used Soviet-style central planning to put investment into heavy industry.

a.q: Which choice best describes the main aim of the first Five-Year Plan?
opts: Build heavy industry through central planning
Hand land from landlords to peasants
Invite public criticism of the party
Form farming communes across the country
a.why: The plan set state targets and put most investment into heavy industry. Land transfer to peasants was land reform, which was a different policy.
a.clue: Think about steel, coal and machinery.

b.q: A new steelworks opens in Anshan in 1955 with Soviet engineers and equipment. What does this show about the plan?
opts: It relied on Soviet help to build heavy industry
It cut ties with the Soviet Union to work alone
It aimed to put most investment into small farms
It left output targets to private business owners
b.why: Soviet advisers and equipment helped build large factories such as steelworks. The plan did not cut ties with the Soviets, and the state, not private owners, set targets.

a.best: Build heavy industry through central planning

b.best: It relied on Soviet help to build heavy industry

problems.detail: Anshan was not a new steelworks in 1955. It was an existing steel centre, built in the Japanese era, that was rebuilt and expanded with Soviet help, with major projects finished from 1953. Better wording would be 'a new mill opens at the Anshan steelworks' or 'the Anshan steelworks is expanded'.

The stem says the steelworks has Soviet engineers and equipment, and the clue asks who sent the engineers. A student can match 'Soviet' to the right option without understanding the plan, which is very easy for Year 12.

proposal.title: The first Five-Year Plan
card: The first Five-Year Plan ran from 1953 to 1957. The state set output targets for the whole economy, a method called central planning.
The plan copied the Soviet Union's model. It put most investment into heavy industry, such as steel, coal and machinery.

a.q: Which choice best describes the main aim of the first Five-Year Plan?

Invite public criticism of the party
Form farming communes across the country
a.why: The plan set state targets and put most investment into heavy industry. Land transfer to peasants was land reform, which was a different policy.
a.clue: Think about steel, coal and machinery.

b.q: In 1955 Chinese planners can fund one project: expanding the Anshan steelworks, a new textile factory, or farm irrigation. Under the first Five-Year Plan, which was most likely to be funded?
opts: The steelworks expansion, as heavy industry came first
The textile factory, as light industry came first
The farm irrigation, as food supply came first
The project that private investors chose to back
b.why: The plan put most investment into heavy industry such as steel, so the steelworks came first. Irrigation is tempting because most Chinese people were peasants, but farming received far less investment and the plan did little to raise farm output.
b.clue: Which kind of industry did the plan rank above all others?

a.best: Build heavy industry through central planning

b.best: The steelworks expansion, as heavy industry came first
